Not a family name: the Library of Congress country study (reopened) and Champion (1996) show Ngarta as the first name François Tombalbaye took in place of his European one during the authenticity campaign of 1973; his family name stayed Tombalbaye. Champion's gloss, Sara ngar « chief », is about that chosen name. No source opened shows Ngarta borne as a surname. As for PAT_NGARLEJY, the reclassification rulings need the name in the family-name position, so the PAT_FADICCA precedent applies. Withdrawn with no successor.

No source tells anything about the name Kigozi. Its only source, the 2016 ruling of the High Court of Uganda (reopened), names John Kigozi Ssebaggala, Prime Minister of the Fumbe clan. Its citation, Nakitende & Another v Kigozi & 2 Others, files him under Kigozi, as it files the first applicant, Nakitende Scovia, under Nakitende: that is the slot a law report keeps for a party's surname, and the one sign of Kigozi in a family-name position. It is one living person's name in one citation: the ruling does not say whether Kigozi is a personal name, a name of the Fumbe clan or a name passed on, and the totemic-clan class had no source. The Ganda personal names the corpus keeps and files as non-hereditary (PAT_LUBEGA, PAT_MUKASA, PAT_KATO) each rest on a source that describes the name; none does here, so the precedent is PAT_KOUM, withdrawn because nothing beyond one bare attestation backed it. Withdrawn with no successor; its Baganda link goes with it. Whether a citation's party name is enough to keep it as a Ganda personal name is left to the operator.
